slides.title: From explanation to executable evidence
body: Week 09 / H2 / guided notebook
Freeze choices before inspecting final errors.
slides.teach: H2 is15minutes explanation then45guided practice. Retrieve H1 distinction between mixture and mechanism change. No API or GPU is required. Students need the practice notebook or the walkthrough at the top of the exercise notebook, not both executions.

slides.title: One row is an independent observation
body: 500 synthetic rows; three dimensionless inputs.
The response has synthetic response units.
slides.teach: Explain this IID synthetic setting before using a random split. Real rows repeated by machine, patient or time require group or chronological rules. x2 is a negative control; do not invent physical units for these variables.

slides.title: Write the generator explicitly
body: y = 2*x0 + x1 squared + noise.
Noise SD is 0.2; x2 is unused.
slides.teach: Use known synthetic mechanism to make representation errors interpretable. No claim of discovering a physical law is made. The relation is stipulated, not inferred from held-out labels.

slides.title: The linear model lacks a basis term
body: Scaling does not create x1 squared.
Add the basis term before standardization.
slides.teach: Explain standardization as affine transformation, incapable of creating a square. The fixed feature mapping uses no labels. Ridgealpha1 and solverSVD are shared. The expanded model is predeclared because the synthetic generator is known.

slides.title: Reserve the final test once
body: 350 train; 75 validation; 75 test.
Keep row identities disjoint and exhaustive.
slides.teach: Training fits parameters and scaler. Validation selects candidate by MAE. Final test estimates performance after decisions. Reusing test outcomes to change a candidate invalidates its role as untouched final evidence.

slides.title: Select by a predeclared rule
body: Lowest validation MAE wins.
Exact ties favour the simpler linear model.
slides.teach: The tie rule must be fixed before inspection. We report both candidates as a predeclared comparison, without reselecting on final test. Do not refit on train+validation in this particular replay protocol, which reproduces training-only fits.

slides.title: Stress one input distribution
body: Keep fitted parameters, base rows and noise.
Scale only x1 and recompute the target.
slides.teach: Use three minutes to distinguish paired conditions from independently regenerated datasets. Pairing reduces irrelevant comparison variation but does not eliminate uncertainty or establish deployment robustness. The target mechanism stays fixed while its inputs change.

slides.title: Open a free CPU notebook
body: Use Colab or local Jupyter.
Run the walkthrough once from the top.
payload: # No API key, no GPU, no external data
slides.teach: Practice begins. Link to the complete notebook in the toolbar. Pairs alternate driver and reviewer. If using the exercise notebook, its first26cells already contain the full walkthrough; do not double-run both notebooks.

slides.title: Record actual environment versions
body: A seed alone is not an experiment identity.
Keep configuration, data hash and versions.
slides.teach: Ask students to copy or retain the printed ENV and CONFIG automatically exported later. Package versions are recorded, not silently claimed pinned across all platforms. Minor cross-environment numerical differences must be evaluated with a stated tolerance.

slides.title: Verify the split assertions
body: No overlap; all 500 rows accounted for.
Random splitting is justified only by this IID setup.
slides.teach: Teaching fragment, the runnable notebook checks all three pairwise overlaps and exact sizes. Students inspect actual shapes. If assertion fails, stop before fitting; do not bypass checks to obtain a score.

slides.title: Freeze the CSV before selecting
body: Store row ID, split, features and target.
Keep SHA-256 alongside the result.
slides.teach: Open the file panel and inspect the schema. Do not edit to improve scores. A checksum authenticates bytes relative to a recorded value, not correctness of labels or permission to make a scientific claim.

slides.title: Fit transformations on training only
body: The pipeline owns the scaler and Ridge fit.
Validation and test only call predict.
payload: # Never fit a scaler on all 500 rows.
slides.teach: Have the reviewer locate the training-only fit in the notebook. The label-free quadratic map is fixed but the scaler parameters are learned. This separates a predetermined basis from a data-fitted preprocessing step.

slides.title: Inspect the validation comparison
body: Read actual MAE, not a promised score.
Record the selected candidate before continuing.
slides.teach: Actual CPU reference output for this frozen dataset. The quadratic candidate wins validation in this reference execution; students must report their own actual run. Check validation n75 and tie rule rather than selecting by final-test results.

slides.title: Now open final test evidence
body: Compare MAE and RMSE on the same 75 rows.
The selected candidate remains frozen.
slides.teach: Actual predeclared two-candidate reference comparison. Explain why RMSE is at least MAE. Reference values are approximately linearMAE1.032 and quadraticMAE.164, but use full JSON precision for replication. Do not call these deployment results.

slides.title: Reconcile subgroup counts and totals
body: Predeclared extreme slice: abs(x1) > 1.
The two slice counts must add to 75.
slides.teach: Students recompute weighted MAE from both slice means and counts and compare to total. Counts are visible on plot labels. The predeclared boundary is1; later threshold sweeps are exploratory only.

slides.title: Inspect the linear residual pattern
body: Negative tails suggest a missing curved term.
Check the residual sign before interpretation.
slides.teach: Use the actual held-out scatter. Compare its curvature to H1 analytic1-x1^2; the fitted model has noise and fitted coefficients, so it is not identical to that curve. Ask for one observed tail case rather than a vague description.

slides.title: Inspect the expanded-model residuals
body: Adding the known square removes much structure.
A smaller pattern is not proof of correctness.
slides.teach: Compare residual structure while attending to axis scales. The two automatically scaled plots do not share y limits; students should compare numerical errors, not just vertical occupied space. Remaining noise and finite fitting effects are expected.

slides.title: Use parity to locate large errors
body: The diagonal means prediction equals observation.
Distance from it is the signed residual vertically.
slides.teach: The same75test observations appear for both candidates. Ask students which response region the linear model underpredicts. The diagonal is a reference, not a fitted trend line. Metric evidence should accompany visual impressions.

slides.title: Relate a pattern to a known mechanism
body: Subtract the known 2*x0 contribution.
The remaining training response follows a square.
slides.teach: This diagnostic uses a known generating coefficient in a synthetic teaching problem. It is not an observational discovery method or validation-driven feature search. Distinguish training dots from the analytic known-term curve.

slides.title: Run paired stress scales 1, 1.5, 2.5
body: Keep all candidate fits frozen.
Compare actual errors across the new populations.
slides.teach: The stress curves are actual fixed-model outputs on the same paired 150-row base cohort. Input scaling exposes the omitted square in the linear candidate. Read the actual reference values and do not generalize an exact error ratio to arbitrary models or deployment shifts.

slides.title: Input drift is visible without labels
body: The stress x1 distribution is broader.
This plot alone does not measure model error.
slides.teach: These empirical histograms show changed input distributions with sample-dependent bins. The figure is not a formal detection test and does not directly measure prediction error. Pair an input alert with new outcomes to evaluate consequences.

slides.title: Read the high-response stress failures
body: Compare both candidates with the parity line.
Identify one large underprediction.
slides.teach: Use the actual scale-2.5 population. Identify one underpredicted high-response point and find its row in the predictions CSV. Correct representation of the synthetic square helps here, but does not prove robustness against all real shifts.

slides.title: A mean does not show the error tail
body: The CDF shows fractions below each error.
Read a percentile only within observed evidence.
slides.teach: Define the empirical CDF as the fraction of 150 absolute residuals at or below a horizontal error value. Each candidate uses the same outcomes. A finite-sample percentile is not a guaranteed deployment tolerance or an external confidence bound.

slides.title: Inspect training-range flags
body: Dashed lines mark observed min and max.
An outside point may deserve investigation.
slides.teach: Colors indicate input range flags, not correct/incorrect classes. Gaussian support is not bounded by observed min/max. This plot shows the linear model only; do not assign its error magnitudes to the expanded candidate.

slides.title: Read uncertainty with its conditioning
body: Intervals resample fixed-model slice errors.
Counts and IID assumptions remain essential.
slides.teach: These descriptive intervals resample fixed-model residuals 300 times within each slice. They condition on the fitted model and omit training and arbitrary future-shift uncertainty. Small counts and sampling assumptions remain important.

slides.title: Turn coefficients back into input units
body: Undo standardization before interpretation.
Verify the explicit equation against predict.
slides.teach: Compare known synthetic coefficients with the expanded candidate in original feature coordinates. The true linear coefficients on x1 and x2 are zero, but finite fitted coefficients need not be exactly zero. This explains a fitted function, not real causal effects.

slides.title: Task 2: run the boundary sweep
body: Use abs(x1) thresholds 0.5, 1 and 1.5.
Record each group count with its actual MAE.
slides.teach: Execute Task 2 in the exercise notebook. Verify that each pair of slice counts adds to 75. Label the sweep exploratory. A favourable boundary found after examining final-test labels cannot support a newly unbiased performance claim.

slides.title: Save the guided checkpoint
body: Keep metrics JSON, predictions CSV and ZIP.
H3 reuses frozen data and models.
slides.teach: Locate week09-reliability-evidence.zip in the Files panel. It contains the actual reference outputs, not completed student answers. Identify the correct run by configuration ID and data hash. Download it before the runtime ends.

slides.title: Summary: choices and evidence differ
body: Validation selects; final test evaluates.
Stress diagnosis keeps the fitted model fixed.
slides.teach: Pairs explain the distinction between validation selection, final evaluation and frozen-model stress diagnosis. Correct the misconception that choosing the best final-test score leaves the test unbiased. The synthetic reference is not deployment validation.

slides.title: Exit: name a reproducible checkpoint
body: Show your data hash and selected candidate.
State one observed failure and one limitation.
slides.teach: Show the actual data hash, selected candidate, one observed failure and one limitation in a one-minute explanation. If the evidence ZIP is missing, recover that checkpoint before proceeding to H3.
